name: fish

attributes.attribute: made by rubbing planks of wood

sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: A fragment about a famine joins a protective fire ritual. In County Limerick, dancers received a tap from a cut reed to ward off illness. The reeds went into a fire, where the contagion burned away. Dancers leapt over the flames. People then used the ashes to bless their harvest and livestock. In Scotland, flame shielded and cleansed at the same time. One ritual carried a flame around a house, moving sunwise, to guard the building and its people. When famine or epidemic threatened, the need-fire served. Each hearth in that area was put out. A team of men rubbed planks of wood to strike a flame. Each family took a flame from the fresh fire home. The men doused the old fire and spread its ashes on cattle for protection.

okr.objective: The fish entry records the protective fire ritual and the need-fire.
key_results: The reeds were tossed into a fire to burn away illness.
Fire carried sunwise guarded a Scottish house.
The need-fire answered famine or epidemic.
Plank of wood rubbing struck the new flame.
